To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effective microvasculature permeability of albuminevans blue is high even in slowly-growing tumors, poorly-angiogenic tumors and tumors with low VEGF-expression.

the effective microvessel permeability to albumin is high in human melanoma xenografts, that this permeability is not related to tumor volumeric growth rate, angiogenesis rate, or VEGFF expression, and that the three last-mentioned factors differ significantly among the melanomas.
the effective microvascula permeability of macomolecules can be high in tumors showing low VVEGF expression, low angiogenic activity, and slow growth rate.

the regulation of microvascular permeability to macromolecules in human melanoma xenotransplants.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective microvessel permeability of albumins is not regulated in melanoma xenografted in athymic nude mice.

the microvascular permeabilities to macromolecules of the human melanomas used here are high compared with the values measured for other tumor types, but the permeabilities do not correlate with tumor volumetric growth, angiogenesis, or vascular endothelial growth factors.
tumor microvascular permeability to albumin-EV is not regulated by tumor growth rate, tumor-induced angiogenesis, or expression of VEGF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effective microvessel permeability of tumors is regulated independently of the tumor's growth rate, rate or extent of angiogenesis, and the expression of vascular endothelium growth factor.
the effective microvasculature permeability to macromolecules is not regulated by the rate of tumor growth, the rate of tumor-induced angiogenesis, or the expression of VEGF.
the effective microvasculature permeability of macronutrients is not a major determinant of tumor growth rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microvascular permeabilities to macromolecules of tumors with different growth rates, angiogenic properties, and VEGE expression are not regulated by the same mechanism.
the effective microvascula permeability of macromanolecules is not necessarily related to the tumor volumetric growth or the rate of tumor growth or angiogenesis or VEGF.
the microvascular permeabilities measured in this study are higher than those reported in the literature for other experimental tumors.
